title: Chapter 3 Quiz 2
description: Naming things, declaring variables, and what a data structure is.
instructions: Chapter 3: Declarations, identifiers and data structures.
Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What is an **identifier**?
options: The operator that gives a value to a name
The data type of a variable or function
The value stored in a constant or variable
The name of a constant, variable or function
questions.explanation: Result, Letter and Conversion_BCD are identifiers: names chosen by the programmer.

questions.question: Which of these are identifiers (names) and not values?
options: Avg_Grade
'John'
Total
StudentName
questions.explanation: Identifiers are names. Watch out: 'John' is a string value and 3.14 is a number, even though they look like words or digits.

questions.question: To declare a variable A of type Integer we write: Declare A {{1}} Integer
questions.explanation: The syntax is Declare VariableName As VariableType.

questions.question: Which line correctly declares a string variable called StudentName?
options: Let StudentName As String
Declare StudentName As String
Declare String As StudentName
Declare StudentName ← String
questions.explanation: Declare VariableName As VariableType. Watch out: the name comes first, then the type.

questions.question: In Declare Age As Integer, which word is the name of the variable?
questions.explanation: Age is the identifier. Integer is the type.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a **function** and a **procedure**?
options: A function has no parameters; a procedure has
A procedure is longer; a function is shorter
A procedure runs once; a function runs often
A function returns a result; a procedure does not
questions.explanation: Both perform a set of actions, but only a function provides a result.

questions.question: A **data structure** is…
options: A group of loops used to repeat code
A file saved on the hard disk drive
A single variable holding one number
Organized data together with operations on it
questions.explanation: Data Structure = Organized Data + Operations on the data.

questions.question: Match each operation on data structures to what it does.
questions.explanation: These are operations listed in the course.

questions.question: Which operation adds a **new element** to an existing collection?
options: Traversal
Merging
Deletion
Insertion
questions.explanation: Insertion adds an element. Watch out: merging combines two whole sorted files, it does not add one element.

questions.question: Sorting only applies to numbers.
questions.explanation: Numbers are sorted in ascending or descending order, and text in alphabetical order. Watch out: alphabetical order is sorting too.
